name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with connective tissue disease

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in Caucasian and Asian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: 2015 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 25 mmHg at rest measured by right heart catheterization
Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) ≤ 15 mmHg to exclude left heart disease
Confirmed diagnosis of underlying connective tissue disease (e.g., systemic sclerosis, systemic lupus erythematosus)
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as chronic thromboembolic disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated mPAP ≥ 25 mmHg with PCWP ≤ 15 mmHg on right heart catheterization plus confirmed connective tissue disease diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Right heart catheterization is mandatory for definitive diagnosis; echocardiography is used for screening and suspicion.

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP indicating right ventricular strain
Autoantibodies consistent with connective tissue disease (e.g., ANA, anti-centromere, anti-Scl-70)
Mild hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: Echocardiography showing right ventricular hypertrophy and elevated pulmonary artery systolic pressure
High-resolution CT scan may show interstitial lung disease associated with connective tissue disease
Ventilation-perfusion scan to exclude chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
other: Right heart catheterization confirming elevated mean pulmonary arterial pressure and pulmonary vascular resistance

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of underlying connective tissue disease

redFlags: Rapid progression of exertional dyspnea and syncope
Signs of right heart failure including peripheral edema and ascites
Severe hypoxemia or cyanosis at rest
